note: HAND-AUTHORED identity rows (#2763, research 0021 E(1)): a name that folds into an IDENTITY (a digest, a pin, a key) is its atom's exact BYTES in every core, never decoded text. Decoding lossily turns every ill-formed run into U+FFFD, so two different wires would read as one value and a digest recomputed over it would pin bytes the wire never carried. A round-trip row is a RECIPE over a base wire: replace ONE name atom's leading bytes with an ill-formed run of the same length (FF, FE, C3 28, FF FE FD), so framing is untouched. The base is REFERENCED from its source vector (base_ref: file, dotted path to a row list, the row's name, the hex field), never copied, so a change to the source reaches these rows by construction. Derive each row: take the base, find the utf-8 bytes of substitute.atom, and replace its Nth occurrence (1-based, wire order) with substitute.with_hex. EXPECTED in every core: the base and every row DECODE and RE-ENCODE BYTE-IDENTICALLY to their own wire (the base is the control, checked first), and a row naming collides_with decodes to a value DIFFERENT from that row's: the two differ only in an ill-formed byte that a lossy decoder maps to the same U+FFFD.

param_names.rule: A param identity's parameter names are a SET of wire atoms, compared as BYTES: two names are the same parameter only when their bytes are equal (#2763 A1c). Decode the requirement's identity (items[1] of Tuple[Atom("at_least"), identity]) with the core's identity decoder. The BASE carries a real duplicate (both names are org.example/b) and is REFUSED in every core: that is the control, checked first. Derive each row by applying EVERY entry of `substitutes` to the base, each occurrence counted in the BASE (1-based). expect=accept: the identity decodes, and its canonical bytes equal the wire's identity bytes. expect=refuse: the identity decoder refuses. A decoder that compares names as lossily decoded text sees FE and FF as one U+FFFD and refuses distinct_ill_formed_names.

closure_producer_version.rule: A closure certificate's producer version is an IDENTITY (it folds into a pin, a digest or a selection), so it is the atom's exact BYTES in every core, never decoded text (#2763 B). Derive each row by replacing the Nth occurrence (1-based, in the BASE) of substitute.atom's UTF-8 bytes with substitute.with_hex, the same length. Decode the wire with the codec, take the value at value_path (empty: the whole wire), decode it with the section's decoder, and re-encode it: the bytes must equal the codec encoding of that value (the base first, as the control). A row's value must differ from the base's, so the substitution landed inside the carrier; and a row naming collides_with decodes to a value different from that row's.

analysis_order.rule: Analysis orders predicates by their BYTES in every core (#2763 C; seat:caa's Q2: a latent tri-core parity defect). rs and go order the dependency edges by (from, to, negated) over the predicates' bytes, and the edges reach the analysis digest in that order. JS strings compare by UTF-16 code units, which is not bytewise order where a supplementary-plane character (U+10000 and above) meets one in U+E000..U+FFFF: UTF-16 puts the surrogate pair FIRST, UTF-8 bytes put it LAST. Build each program over arity-1 predicates named by hex: a `program` entry with a `body` is the rule head(X) :- body..., each body literal pred(X), negated when `neg` is true; an entry without `body` is the ground fact head(c). Analyze it for the goal goal(X) with the core's production analyze. The dependency edges must equal `edges` in order, each [from_hex, to_hex, negated]; the strata must equal `strata` in order, each stratum's members compared as a set (the wire encodes a stratum as a sorted set); the recursion shape must equal `recursion`.

analysis_predicate_identity.rule: A predicate's identity in analysis is its BYTES (#2763 C): two predicates whose names differ only in an ill-formed byte are two predicates. Decoding lossily maps both p\xff (70 FF) and p\xfe (70 FE) to p U+FFFD, so a dependency graph keyed on decoded names merges them into one node: a positive edge between them reads as a self-loop (recursion), and a negation between them reads as a negative cycle, which analysis refuses. Same recipe and the same pins as analysis_order; every row must analyze.

cone_predicate_identity.rule: The cone of a goal is keyed by its predicates' BYTES (#2763 C). The recursion shape of the clauses the goal reaches through body dependencies ranks engines, and a lossy key merges p\xff with p\xfe, so the cone of p\xff would take in p\xfe's recursive rule. Build each program over arity-1 predicates named by hex: a `program` entry with a `body` is the rule head(X) :- body..., each body literal pred(X), negated when `neg` is true; an entry without `body` is the ground fact head(c). Compute the cone's recursion shape for the goal goal(X); it must equal `recursion`.

seal_plan_identity.rule: The certifying producer's SEAL PLAN keys a predicate by its BYTES (#2763 C2; seat:caa's ruling: the load-bearing site, because the function-symbol floor a request needs is computed from this plan). Two predicates whose names differ only in an ill-formed byte (p\xff = 70 FF, p\xfe = 70 FE) are two predicates: a lossy key merges them, so one predicate's clauses count as reached, ruled or sealed for the other. Build each program as in analysis_order (arity-1 predicates named by hex; an entry with a `body` is the rule head(X) :- body, each literal pred(X), negated when `neg`; without one it is the ground fact head(c)); an entry with `head_compound` true heads its rule with head(t(X)), an OPEN compound. For the goal goal(X): the syntactic extensional set (predicates only body-less clauses head) must equal `extensional` (hex, compared as a set); the COMPLETE seal (the query's stratum sealed too) over that set must render its relations, sorted by bytes then arity, as `relations_complete`, each name through the one injective escape (#1961's escaped_name, so p\xff renders p%FF); and the function-symbol level a request needs must equal `level` under an untrusted request, a certifiable one (the prefix seal) and a certifiable one asking for a certified answer set (the complete seal).

undefined_predicate_name.rule: The undefined-predicate diagnostic names each predicate name/arity, the name through the one injective escape (#2984 sites 1 and 2; #1961's ruling, the escaped_name section above). It is text a reader sees, and the CLI's machine sink carries it as its predicate field, so two predicates whose names differ only in an ill-formed byte (p\xff = 70 FF, p\xfe = 70 FE) must never render as one, as a lossy decode renders both p U+FFFD. Build each program as in analysis_order. For the goal goal(X), under the standard theory with no declared extensional set, the undefined predicates, in the diagnostic's order (by name bytes, then arity), must render exactly as `undefined`: rs through UndefinedPredicate's Display, go through its String, ts through undefinedPredicateKey.

pin_mismatch_binding.rule: A pinned certifiable offer whose theory list differs from the required check profile's is refused on the guarantee axis by the theory check, whose cause carries that check's two operands (#2734, seat:caa's operand rule; #2984 site 4): `required_operand_hex` is the required profile's theory list and `offered_operand_hex` the offer's pinned one, each the codec bytes of Tuple[Atom("theories"), list], the list tagged with its slot (seat:caa's self-describing-operand condition) and each binding Tuple[Atom(id), Atom(version), Atom(hex config digest)]. The bytes are the binding's own, so two bindings that differ only in an ill-formed byte are two operands, never one. Before #2734 this section pinned the refusal's prose, which ruling D2 took off the wire. The spec is the demo spec (demo/lt@1.0.0 as its one theory, demo/edge-leaves@1.0.0 leaves, core/always-admit@1.0.0 admit, limits 100000/4096, all config digests zero, the current checker feature set), with its one theory replaced by `offered` for the offer and by `required` for the requirement, each with a zero config digest. The offer's pins are that spec's pins serving the spec's own term identity. Admitting the required spec must fail on the theory check with exactly these operands.
